html:
The potato was first domesticated by farmers in the Andes of southern Peru and northwestern Bolivia, near Lake Titicaca, between about 8000 and 5000 BCE.

Wild potatoes are bitter and often toxic. Over thousands of years, Andean farmers bred hundreds of varieties suited to different heights, soils and frosts. They invented chuño, potatoes freeze-dried in the cold nights and hot days of the high plains, which keep for years. Potatoes, with llamas and the grain quinoa, fed the Tiwanaku, Wari and Inca states, and filled the Inca storehouses.

After the Spanish conquest, the potato reached Europe in the 1570s. It gave more food per acre than grain and helped populations grow from Ireland to Russia and China. Today it is one of the world's main food crops, and Peru keeps thousands of native varieties.
sum: The potato was first domesticated by farmers in the Andes of southern Peru and northwestern Bolivia, near Lake Titicaca, between about 8000 and 5000 BCE.
